options: Adding more machines to share the load
Adding more resources (CPU, RAM) to a single existing machine
Splitting a dataset across multiple machines
Routing requests through a load balancer
questions.explain: Vertical scaling, or 'scaling up,' means giving the one machine you have more resources rather than adding more machines.

questions.q: Why is horizontal scaling described as the distributed-systems answer to growth, rather than vertical scaling?
options: Horizontal scaling is always cheaper per machine
Horizontal scaling doesn't hit the same hard ceiling as vertical scaling, and also improves fault isolation
Vertical scaling is not possible on cloud providers
Horizontal scaling removes the need for a load balancer
questions.explain: Vertical scaling eventually runs out of bigger machines to rent; horizontal scaling can keep adding machines, and spreading load across more machines also means one failing is less damaging.

questions.q: What role does a load balancer play in horizontal scaling?
options: It splits a database into shards
It routes incoming requests across a pool of servers so the added machines are actually used
It increases the RAM of a single server
It guarantees zero latency between machines
questions.explain: Without a load balancer distributing requests, adding more servers wouldn't help — some would sit idle while others stay overloaded.

questions.q: What problem does sharding (partitioning) solve that simply adding more stateless web servers does not?
options: It makes a single machine run faster
It scales data: splitting a dataset across machines so no single machine needs to hold everything
It removes the need for a shard key
It eliminates the need for redundancy entirely
questions.explain: Stateless compute can be multiplied freely because any server can answer any request, but data has to actually be split across machines by a shard key — that's sharding.

questions.q: A load balancer sits in front of ten web servers, but there is only one load balancer in the whole system. What does Lesson 2's terminology call this load balancer?
options: A shard key
A failover replica
A single point of failure
A vertical scaling strategy
questions.explain: Even though it enables horizontal scaling, an unreplicated load balancer is itself a single point of failure — if it goes down, none of the ten servers behind it can be reached.
